component.name: VoLum
component.summary: Guitar amplifier and NAM model player, alone or inside a DAW

description.p: VoLum loads neural amp captures in the .nam format - the same models the Neural Amp Modeler project trains - and puts them where a guitar signal goes: a clean boost, an overdriven pre, a cabinet, and the effects around them. Two hundred and forty-nine captures come with it, from clean Fenders to high-gain Marshalls, and a capture you trained yourself drops into its rig browser.

This package is the stand-alone program: it opens its own window, picks its own audio device, and needs no host. The same window is what a DAW shows when it loads the VST3 bundle in `~/.vst3`, so the amp sounds and behaves the same either way.

On Linux it is X11 (it runs on a Wayland desktop through XWayland), talks to ALSA, and asks the desktop's own portal for its file, folder and colour dialogs rather than dragging a toolkit into a host's process.

screenshot.caption: VoLum's window: amp, rig list and level columns

description.p: First packaged Linux build of this port: the stand-alone as one AppImage, and the VST3 bundle as a zip, both carrying the same 249 bundled captures.

Measured, not assumed: the audio path, the editor window, host-side resizing, the desktop's portal dialogs and the IN/OUT level columns are each checked by a headless run in CI or by a script that counts lit pixels in the package's own window.
